description.purpose: An organisation as a namespace: a name, a boundary, and one open container its members are instantiated into. Nothing else. A level owns what its siblings must share, and the members of one organisation share a name and a boundary -- they do not share a memory, an identity, a broker or a firewall, because under GH #122 the memory belongs to the MEMBER and a group is an audience, not a holder. The level is therefore deliberately thin: its value is the namespace, not the contents, and it should not be padded to look substantial. Since 1.3.0 two more lanes cross it. Outward, `pack_ack` ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)): the receipt of an identity pushed into a generation below, which nothing at this level consumes. Inward, `in_import` ([#467](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/467)): one part of a memory document on its way back into the hive of the member it belongs to, the return leg of `in_export`. Both fall out of the union rule and are declared for that reason alone -- adding a lane in either direction is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 1.4.0 one more crosses it: `mutation_committed`, the mutation door's receipt, carried into `./members` by this level's twentieth edge (GH #553). A level that declares the lane takes part in it and may not be skipped.
description.use_when: One per organisation, instantiated into the shell's orgs container. Use it whenever two or more members should answer under one name and share nothing but that name -- a company, a household, a team, a customer. Instantiate it in the mutation that also wires its transit lanes: one edge per accepted lane onto the hive path, and one per emitted lane from the hive path to whoever asked. The hive is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No memory of its own, and this is a ruling rather than an omission: 'what does the group know about X' is a filter on the read, never a second store -- two stores would force the writer to decide which one a sentence belongs to before extraction has run, which is not a decision it can make. A group that owns an agent nobody owns personally is a MEMBER with its own name, instantiated from member like any other. No identity, no broker, no firewall, no sink, no drain: each of those belongs either to a member below or to the shell above. No cells at all -- an org that grows a cell has stopped being a namespace.
examples: PORTS - the hive path IS the address, and the level is deliberately OPEN (`params.ports` is absent, not empty): the mutation that instantiates a member into the container draws edges to that member, and a seal would refuse exactly those endpoints. Entry (on hop.route, all onto the org's own path): 'in_turn' a turn for a member, 'in_recall' a question against a member's memory, 'in_brief' a read of a member's curated record, 'in_propose' a write against it, 'in_build_result' the baumeister's answer on its way home, 'in_export' a demand that a member's memory be handed out as a document, 'in_import' one part of such a document on its way back into the hive it belongs to. Exits (all leaving the hive path): 'answer', 'bundle' (the answer to a question asked at a member's own 'in_recall' door, GH #533 -- the question crossed this level from the day it shipped and the answer had nowhere to go), 'ack', 'reject', 'error', 'build', 'close_report', 'export_done', plus the four a member re-emits on behalf of its assistants -- 'write', 'turn_write', 'prune', 'pack_ack'. Nothing is translated on the way through -- a namespace carries hop and context untouched.

the whole of the level's behaviour is transit, and the edge set is one line long: one door `.` -> `./members` per accepted lane, one exit `./members` -> `.` per emitted lane, and nothing else. There is nothing below the container to route to until a member is instantiated, and that mutation draws the member's own edges.

WHERE THE LANES COME FROM: they are the union of what the level's occupant accepts and emits at the version pinned in each `because`, minus the lanes a sibling inside the level consumes itself. Nothing is subtracted here, because the only thing inside an org is the container. If a member ever moves a lane, this level moves with it in the same commit -- `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh302_org_is_a_namespace.rs` reads both files and fails until it does. That is not hypothetical: `write`, `turn_write` and `prune` arrived here the day the member started re-emitting what its assistants raise and nothing at member level consumes.

the lane that is deliberately ABSENT is 'turn'. A member consumes its own turn internally (`./channels` -> `./firewall` since GH #454) and never emits one, so an org that declared it would carry an exit edge that can never fire -- an interface promising something no occupant produces.

instantiating an organisation: one add_nodes with template 'org@1.4.0', plus the transit edges. Nothing is registered as a cell by that mutation -- both directories are hive scopes, and a hive is a scope marker, not an actor.

adding a member afterwards: an add_nodes into <org>/members with the 'member' template at a pinned version, and in the SAME mutation the pass-through edges the member needs. The container is open precisely so that this mutation is legal.

the container's unbound behaviour is UNDECLARED, on purpose: the slot of GH #285 governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so a slot declaration on this level could never fire. A message reaching an empty container takes the ordinary path. Read out of `unbound_slot_behaviour` in `crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs`, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope.

what would make this level fat, and is therefore refused: an org-level memory hive, an org-level identity, an org-wide firewall, a shared drain. Each of them belongs to a member or to the shell -- see the README.
